newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-SEEDS KEEP FALLING IN MONTE CARLO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SEEDS KEEP FALLING IN MONTE CARLO.

text.p: Seeds kept falling at the Monte Carlo Open on Wednesday as more leading figures of the hard court game failed to adapt to clay.
Five more favourites crashed out of the first major European tournament of the season, hard on the heels of the surprising losses on Tuesday of top seeds Pete Sampras and Thomas Muster.

American Jim Courier, Sweden's Thomas Enqvist, South African Wayne Ferreira, Swiss Marc Rosset and, more surprisingly Spanish claycourt specialist Alberto Berasategui followed Sampras, Muster and Boris Becker on the way out.
The defeats left Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek, impressive conqueror of Germany's Michael Stich, Chile's Marcelo Rios and Spain's Alberto Costa with the best chances for the title.

Krajicek, who had just flown back from Japan after winning in Tokyo last week, was amazingly quick to adapt to the slow surface. His 6-3 6-0 demolition of Stich, losing finalist in the French Open last year, led him to believe in his chances this season on clay.

"I feel pretty good going into the French Open this season. I think I was one of the best players at the French last year. If only I had not felt so tired in the end of my match against Yevgeny (Kafelnikov)," he said.
Russian Kafelnikov, seeded third here, beat him in the quarterfinals in Paris and went on to win that title.
In the third round, Krajicek will meet another big server, Australian Mark Philipoussis, who was too strong for former French Open champion Courier.
The American, seeded eighth, struggled to return the Australian's serve and failed to impose his pace in his 7-5 7-5 loss. A break at the end of each set was enough for Philippoussis to get through.
Fresh from winning in Barcelona on Monday, Alberto Costa crushed Czech Slava Dosedel in straight sets and will face Rios in a rematch of last year's semifinal here.

If the misfortunes of Ferreira against Spain's Carlos Costa or Enqvist against Czech Bohdan Ulihrach could be expected since they are no claycourt fans, the early exits of Rosset and Berasategui were more astonishing.
A semifinalist at the French open last year, Rosset bowed 7-6 6-1 to Czech Daniel Vacek while Berasategui, French runner-up in 1994, lost to compatriot Emilio Alvarez, a qualifier.
